Subject: Aligning hourly peak patterns to committed GPU tiers — StrataGen renewal

Vanessa and team,

Thanks for the renewal materials so far. We ran a quick analysis on Q2 usage and what stands out are sharp hourly spikes tied to batch export jobs and some customer-driven inference bursts. Before we get to numbers on the contract, procurement needs help mapping our observed hourly peaks into committed GPU tiers. Two specific asks:

- Can Redwood translate our 95th-percentile hourly vCPU/GPU usage into recommended committed tranches (and recommended buffer) so we can evaluate cost vs. risk?
- If we need short-term surge capacity (48–72h) during big exports, how would that affect tiers/credits and SLA?

Attached a CSV with weekly hourly heatmaps (stratagen_weekly_hourly_heatmap.csv) and a zipped sample of raw usage snapshots for May–July (usage_snaps_Q2_2026.zip).

We'd like a written playbook and a short walk-through call this week. Can you propose a mapping and a fallback strategy?

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Ops, StrataGen
elaine.park@stratagen.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Aligning hourly peak patterns to committed GPU tiers — StrataGen renewal

Elaine —

Thanks for the data. I pulled the attached playbook (proposed_tiers_v1.pdf) and a concise mapping from the heatmap into three recommended commitment bands: Baseline, Peak, and Surge Buffer. High level:

- Baseline tier (steady-state): covers median sustained capacity during business hours — recommend committing to 60% of avg daily consumption to reduce unit costs while preserving headroom for autoscaling.
- Peak tier (95th-hourly): sized to cover recurring hourly peaks (~95th percentile). We recommend reserving an additional tranche equal to the 95th-hourly rounded up to the nearest tranche size (we use 4‑GPU tranche units).
- Surge buffer (temporary, 48–72h): cover 1.5x of historical one-off export peaks. Implement as burst credits (hourly-billed) with automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model if oversubscription occurs.

Notes on SLA: committing to Peak tier lowers your reliance on burst credits and improves latency SLO during peaks. Burst credits are best-effort but we can include guaranteed short-window capacity for an extra monthly fee; details in the attached PDF.

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal calibration: Ben/Marissa and I will convert your CSV into tranche-aligned numbers.
2) Call: 30–45 minute walkthrough Wednesday 08/26 at 10:30am PT?
3) If accepted, we'll provide a redlined amendment and pro forma pricing for Baseline+Peak tranches and optional Surge credits.

I've attached the heatmap interpretation and the first-pass tranche mapping. If you want a more conservative buffer we'll size Peak+20% as an alternate.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
